No blocking ambiguities found. Proceeding to adversarial planning.

The body is unusually well-specified for a `kind: infra` task: explicit Goal,
a four-file Scope, five numbered Acceptance criteria, and a Notes-for-planner
section. The one genuinely open design question — Acceptance item 3, which
terminal to adopt when the pool stays dry — is **explicitly delegated to the
planner** by the body itself ("Candidates, to be decided by the planner — do
NOT assume the first"), so it is a planning decision, not a clarifier gap.

**Context resolved from project knowledge:**

- **No duplicate / near-duplicate exists.** Registry-wide title scan for
  `model pool` / `model quota` / `quota exhaust` / `fable 5 limit` /
  `subagent model` returns only #2644 itself. The four other `reconciler`
  hits are unrelated and all `completed`: #755 (persist every upheld
  finding), #802 (bug-class sibling sweep), #808 (SPEC.md Lens 12
  contradiction), #1134 (adopt-severe skip). Nothing to fold in or defer to.
- **The gap is confirmed mechanically.** `.claude/rules/context-hygiene.md`
  contains ZERO occurrences of `quota` / `model pool` / `model limit` /
  `usage limit` / `credit`. Its two documented subagent-death ladders are
  refusal rungs (a)-(g) and autocompact-thrash Class 1 / Class 2 only, exactly
  as the body states. The third class does not exist today.
- **A directly mirrorable precedent exists for Acceptance items 3(c) and 4.**
  The Codex-side quota sentinel is real and shipped: `codex_task.py`
  (`QUOTA_SENTINEL_RELPATH = .claude/cache/codex-quota-exhausted-until`,
  exit 9, reason `codex-quota-exhausted`, #1126), the canonical fail-OPEN
  pre-spawn check with its two-sided plausibility window in
  `.claude/rules/codex-ensemble-review.md`, and a watcher pass that observes
  the outage (`autonomous_session_watch.py` `codex_outage_pass`, one deduped
  push per episode, kill switch `EPM_DISABLE_CODEX_OUTAGE_PASS=1`). This also
  answers the body's third Note — the watcher precedent for counting repeated
  quota deaths already exists on the Codex side and can be twinned.
- **Acceptance item 3 partially collides with an EXISTING terminal the
  planner must reconcile with, not re-invent.** `steps/09-step-5.md`
  (~lines 1391-1397) already rules that the Phase-2 adopt-more-severe
  last-resort fail-safe applies to the in-context planner site ONLY, and that
  "at the marker-mode sites here a twice-dead reconciler fails LOUD per the
  Step 5b durable-verdict-first rule (item 4), never adopt-more-severe." So a
  terminal is already asserted; what is missing is its DEFINITION (fails loud
  into what — `epm:failure v1` + `status:blocked`? which `failure_class`?
  which reason token?). The planner should specify that existing terminal
  rather than introduce a competing one, and must not weaken the
  never-adopt-more-severe ruling at marker-mode sites.
- **The durable-verdict-first probe the body asks to restate already exists**
  and is the right anchor: `steps/09-step-5.md` § Step 5b item 4 — a dead
  critic/reconciler is NOT by itself a no-show; probe for a durable verdict
  before any no-show handling fires. The new ladder should reference it, not
  duplicate it.
- **Live blocked consumer.** #2387 is at `status: running` and genuinely
  stuck on this exact wall: `epm:progress` v19-v22 record four consecutive
  Fable 5 model-limit deaths on the round-5 reconciler (21:12:05Z, 21:12:59Z,
  21:24:07Z, 21:55:56Z), each immediate, each with the durable probe
  unchanged at `epm:review-reconcile` versions `[1]` (round-4 only). That is
  the acceptance test in the wild.

**Remaining blocking ambiguities:** none.

**Pacing decision — NOT the 429 ladder.** No immediate minute-boundary retry
and no escalating-hold retry chain was run here. A model-quota pool does not
replenish on a per-minute bucket, so the 429 ladder's "retry anyway at the
~10 min cap" rung cannot succeed against it; #2387 demonstrated that
empirically with three retries in 25 minutes that could not have worked. This
is the pacing gap the task's Scope names, and acting it out again would have
been the documented mistake.

**Discovered rung, recorded because the plan should consider it.** The Codex
lane is a SEPARATE pool and is currently live: the canonical fail-open
sentinel check (`.claude/cache/codex-quota-exhausted-until`) returns
`CODEX_QUOTA_CLEAR` at 22:03:00Z. But note the trap — the `codex-*` twins are
themselves THIN CLAUDE prompt-composers, so under a dry Claude pool they die
before composing and the Codex lane is unreachable THROUGH THEM. It stays
reachable only if the ORCHESTRATOR composes the prompt file itself and
bg-dispatches `scripts/codex_task.py` directly (a Bash call, not a subagent).
That asymmetry is not documented anywhere today and belongs in the ladder.

**Route taken.** `.claude/rules/context-hygiene.md` sanctions orchestrator
inline composition "only for a workflow-fix task fixing this failure mode, or
refusal rung (c)". Task #2644 IS the workflow-fix task fixing this failure
mode, so this session is textually inside that carve-out; the task body
(Acceptance 3(b)) independently flags the same point as a live question. The
plan draft will therefore be composed inline by the orchestrator and the
independence breach disclosed with the fixed `[epm-inline-fallback]` token in
a separate note, per the same rule. A Claude `critic` retry remains owed for
the plan-review floor and will be attempted once the pool recovers.
